tips.title: Mastering Panel Line Scribing with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For crisp panel lines, use RB Productions' scribing tools. First, lightly score the panel line with a pencil to serve as a guide. Then, use the RB Productions 0.5mm scribing tool to create a shallow line. For deeper lines, use the 0.7mm or 1mm tools. Work slowly and steadily, applying gentle pressure. Afterwards, apply a wash or panel line accent to enhance the effect.

tips.title: Bending Photo-Etch with Eduard Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard's photo-etch bending jigs help achieve consistent, accurate bends. Before bending, anneal the photo-etch by heating it with a soldering iron until it glows red, then cool. Place the jig on a flat surface, insert the photo-etch into the jig's groove, and gently bend it over the jig's edge using pliers. For tight bends, use the smaller jigs.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Bearing Cleaner
tips.text: Regularly clean your Iwata airbrush needle to maintain performance. Remove the needle chuck and needle, then soak them in Iwata Bearing Cleaner for 15 minutes. Use a soft brush to gently scrub the needle, then rinse with isopropyl alcohol and dry. Apply a drop of Iwata grease to the needle's point before reinserting.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya vs Kabuki Tapes
tips.text: Tamiya tape is ideal for masking large areas due to its width and adhesion. For intricate masking, Kabuki tape is preferable due to its thinner profile and better conformability. To use Kabuki tape, cut it with a sharp blade held perpendicular to the tape's surface. Apply it with a pen or pick it up with tweezers for precise placement.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression with Arma Hobby and ICM Sanding Sticks
tips.text: For optimal surface preparation, use sanding sticks in a progression from coarse to fine grit. Start with Arma Hobby's P120 grit stick for heavy work, followed by ICM's P240 for general use, and finish with ICM's P400 for final smoothing. Wet sanding is recommended for better control and cleaner results. After sanding, thoroughly wash and dry the model before painting.
